_description: Character sprite prompts v4 for gold visual novel sprites, built from character_prompts_v2.json v2.3 plus the Jordan keeper learnings. Jordan is unchanged from v2.3, it is the locked keeper prompt. The other five prompts were edited only for the learnings below, not rewritten from scratch.
_based_on: character_prompts_v2.json v2.3, and jordan-keeper-v23.jpg plus jordan-keeper-v23.md
_jordan_learnings_applied: Keeper first: save the exact prompt and the keeper image together, name the keeper traits, and compare every later result trait by trait against that pair.
One trait at a time: a prompt that already produced a keeper gets surgical edits only, never a full rewrite.
Describe hair by its outer edge and mass, not by a mood word: a curl cloud needs a bumpy outer edge, smooth closed contours reads as a helmet.
Anchor presentation in words, not pronouns alone: name the jaw, brow, neck, and shoulders, or the model fills the vacuum. For an unspecified character, name androgynous explicitly.
Split the hand pair: hands at different heights, doing different jobs, with side, height, palm direction, and finger shape all named. Never both hands hidden, at waist level, or doing the same thing.
One focal emblem per character: name it, name where its detail stops, and forbid scattered badges, sleeve patches, and all over print, or the model scatters the detail.
Do not fight render style with text: the not 2D illustration instruction failed on Jordan, style follows the reference image and the tool. Keep material language, drop style war language.
Watch prompt length: Jordan v2 was 398 words and v2.3 is 415 words, and length diluted the traits that were working. V4 trims the other five prompts while keeping every lock.
One text only attempt for a stubborn trait, then rerun the identical prompt with the keeper image as the reference instead of rewriting the wording again.
_keeper_rules: Change one trait at a time from a keeper prompt. Run one generation after each single edit and compare it directly with the keeper image. Keep the version that preserves the most keeper traits. Stop iterating a trait when the result matches the keeper on that trait.
_generation_workflow: 1. Use the same reference image and settings that produced the keeper for that character. 2. Run one trait change at a time. 3. Compare silhouette, hair edge, face, hand pair, focal emblem, and framing against the keeper. 4. If a trait fails on a text only run, rerun with the keeper image as reference before editing words again.
